explanation: The word means 'flower viewing'. In the 700s it usually meant plum blossoms, brought from China, before cherry blossoms took over in the Heian period.

claims.text: Hanami is the Japanese custom of enjoying cherry blossoms in spring, often with picnics beneath the trees.
Hanami does not refer to picnicking beneath wisteria, magnolias or lotus flowers.
In the 8th century (the Nara period), flower viewing in Japan usually meant plum blossoms, introduced from China.
Cherry blossoms became the main flowers of hanami in the Heian period (794 to 1185).
